'''''Anigozanthos rufus''''' is a grass-like [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant]] native to the southern coasts of [[Western Australia]]. Common names include '''red kangaroo paw''',<ref name=FloraBase/> '''crimson kangaroo paw''',<ref name=austseed>{{cite web|url=https://www.australianseed.com/shop/item/anigozanthos-rufus|title=''Anigozanthos rufus'' Crimson Kangaroo Paw|accessdate=24 May 2020|publisher=Australian Seed}}</ref> and '''backdraft'''.<ref name=anp/>

==Description==
The red kangaroo paw grows to a height of {{cvt|0.2|to|1|m}}.<ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|id=1415|title=''Anigozanthos rufus''}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Australian native plants|url=https://www.australianplants.com/plants.aspx?id=1717}}</ref>
The grass-like plant has green and grey flat, strappy leaves that are {{cvt|17|to|28|cm}} long.<ref name=FloraBase/> It produces long red to purple to yellow coloured flowers in spring and early summer from August to January.<ref name=FloraBase/> The tubular flowers have a velvety texture<ref name=kings>{{cite web|url=https://www.bgpa.wa.gov.au/images/horticulture/docs/pn_anigozanthos_rufus.pdf|title=''Anigozanthos rufus'' Kings Park Federation Flame|accessdate=23 May 2020|work=Native Plant Notes|publisher=Kings Park and Botanical Gardens}}</ref> and form dense heads at the end.<ref name=austseed/>
[[File:Kangaroo paw (crimson).png|center|thumb]]

==Taxonomy==
The species was first formally described by the botanist [[Jacques Labillardière]] in 1800 as part of the work ''Relation du Voyage à la Recherche de la Perouse''. Synonyms include ''Schwaegrichenia rufa'', ''Agonizanthos rufa'' and ''Anigozanthos tyrianthinus''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bie.ala.org.au/species/https://id.biodiversity.org.au/node/apni/2915655#names|title=''Anigozanthos rufus'' Labill.|work=Atlas of Living Australia|accessdate=24 May 2020|publisher=[[Global Biodiversity Information Facility]]}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The plant is often situated in seasonally wet areas growing in sandy soils along the south coast from around [[Albany, Western Australia|Albany]] in the west to around [[Cape Arid]] in the east.<ref name=FloraBase/>

==Cultivation==
It is commercially available in pots or seed form<ref name=austseed/> and is suitable for small gardens or as a border plant and is also suitable as a pot plant but needs to be moved indoors for the winter months in cooler areas. Once it is established it is drought tolerant, grows in full sun or shade and moderately frost tolerant. The plant needs space for plenty of air flow around the base to assist to prevent [[Ink disease]] which blackens the leaf blade.<ref name=anp>{{cite web|url=https://www.australianplants.com/plants.aspx?id=1717|title=''Anigozanthos rufus'' Backdraft|accessdate=23 May 2020|publisher=Australian Native Plants}}</ref> Clumps of the plant can be divided in the summer.<ref name=austseed/>
